image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a Rock Beauty fish (Holocanthus tricolor). The image captures the anterior to mid-section of the fish, showing the characteristic black head and front body transitioning into a bright yellow posterior. The eye is visible on the far left edge, and the dorsal and anal fins are partially visible at the top and bottom edges respectively.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small protrusible mouth with brush-like teeth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is located at the very tip of the snout, which is cut off by the left edge of the frame. It is impossible to verify the presence of brush-like teeth or the specific shape of the mouth.
The eye is visible on the far left edge. While partially cropped, the visible portion shows a large, dark pupil and iris consistent with the 'large eyes' description of the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed disc-shaped body with compact proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible curvature of the dorsal and ventral profiles indicates a deep, laterally compressed body typical of angelfish/butterflyfish. The proportions appear correct for the class.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Striking gold and black coloration: anterior body and head black, posterior body and tail golden yellow with black margin.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the diagnostic color pattern: a solid black mask covering the head and anterior body, sharply contrasting with the bright yellow/gold of the posterior body. The transition is distinct and accurate.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Continuous dorsal fin with spiny anterior and soft-rayed posterior portions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is visible along the top edge. It appears continuous from the black region into the yellow region. While individual spines vs. soft rays are hard to distinguish at this resolution, the structural continuity is present.
The anal fin is visible along the bottom edge, mirroring the dorsal fin's position and coloration transition. No structural anomalies are visible.
The tail (caudal fin) is completely outside the frame on the right side. It cannot be evaluated.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The background is heavily blurred (bokeh), which is expected in macro photography but can sometimes mask AI generation errors. The edges of the fish show slight softness, likely due to depth-of-field rather than generation artifacts, but warrants scrutiny for edge bleeding.

The texture on the black scales appears slightly uniform/smooth compared to the more detailed yellow scales. This could be lighting/shadow or a minor textural inconsistency common in AI generations, but it is subtle.
